title: Grade 3 Math — Mon, Jun 23
description: Fractions — Day 1 of 5: Introduction — equal parts, numerator, denominator
subject: mathematics

questions.question: A pizza is cut into 4 equal parts. Ravi eats 1 part. What fraction did Ravi eat?
questions.explanation: Ravi ate 1 out of 4 equal parts. The fraction is 1/4 (one-fourth). The top number (1) is the numerator; the bottom number (4) is the denominator.

questions.question: In the fraction 3/8, what is the numerator?
questions.explanation: In any fraction, the number on top is called the numerator. In 3/8, the numerator is 3.

questions.question: In the fraction 5/7, what is the denominator?
questions.explanation: In any fraction, the number on the bottom is the denominator. In 5/7, the denominator is 7 — it tells us the total number of equal parts.

questions.question: A chocolate bar is broken into 6 equal pieces. Sita eats 2 pieces. What fraction did she eat?
questions.explanation: Sita ate 2 out of 6 equal pieces. The fraction is 2/6 (two-sixths).

questions.question: For a fraction to be valid, the parts must be:
options: Any size
Equal in size
Different shapes
Decreasing in size
questions.explanation: For fractions to work, the whole must be divided into EQUAL parts. Unequal parts cannot be represented by a single fraction.

questions.question: Which fraction means 'one whole' (all parts taken)?
questions.explanation: When the numerator equals the denominator (like 5/5), it equals 1 whole. All parts are taken.

questions.question: A ribbon is cut into 5 equal pieces. 3 pieces are red and 2 are blue. What fraction is red?
questions.explanation: 3 red pieces out of 5 total equal pieces = 3/5 (three-fifths).

questions.question: A circle is divided into 8 equal parts. 5 parts are shaded. Write the fraction for the UNSHADED part.
What does the denominator tell us?
options: How many parts are taken
How many equal parts the whole is divided into
The size of each part
Which parts are coloured
questions.explanation: The denominator (bottom number) tells us the total number of equal parts the whole has been divided into.

questions.question: Out of 10 students in a group, 4 are girls. What fraction are girls?
questions.explanation: 4 girls out of 10 students = 4/10. The numerator (4) = girls; denominator (10) = total students.

questions.question: A rectangle is divided into 12 equal parts. 7 are shaded. What fraction is NOT shaded?
questions.explanation: Not shaded = 12 − 7 = 5 parts. Fraction not shaded = 5/12.

questions.question: Mera has a bag of 15 marbles. She gives 6 marbles to her friend. What fraction of the marbles did she give away?
questions.explanation: She gave away 6 out of 15 marbles = 6/15.

questions.question: If a fraction has numerator 0 (like 0/5), what does it mean?
options: All parts are taken
No parts are taken — it equals zero
It is not a valid fraction
It equals 1
questions.explanation: 0/5 means 0 parts out of 5 are taken — this equals zero. It is a valid fraction and represents nothing taken from the whole.

questions.question: A square is divided into parts, but NOT equal parts. Priya shades one part. Is this a valid fraction?
options: Yes, any shaded part is a fraction
No — fractions require equal parts; unequal division is not a fraction
Yes, as long as one part is shaded
It depends on the size of the square
questions.explanation: Fractions only work when the whole is divided into EQUAL parts. If the parts are unequal, we cannot name the shaded region as a fraction.

questions.question: Rohan says '3/0 is a fraction because 3 is the numerator and 0 is the denominator.' Is he correct?
options: Yes, it is a valid fraction
No — the denominator cannot be 0; you cannot divide something into 0 parts
Yes — 0 in the denominator makes it 0
Only if the numerator is also 0
questions.explanation: The denominator can NEVER be 0. Division by zero is undefined in mathematics. You cannot divide a whole into 0 equal parts.
